analysis.title: Up and Adam: Chart of the Day: Do Not Fear The Death Cross
key_insights: The S&P 500 fell for a fourth straight session on 11/17/2026, matching its longest losing streak since June, with a 3.4% MTD loss.
MTD weakness is concentrated in Energy (-9.7%) and Technology (-9.4%). Six of 11 sectors are positive MTD.
65% of S&P 500 constituents trade above their 50-day moving averages, versus 23% at the start of October.

The Russell 2000's 50-DMA is on pace to cross below its 200-DMA on 11/18/2026 (a 'death cross'). Over 20 years the signal occurred 13 times, followed by an average 10.4% gain over 12 months and positive returns 77% of the time.
Raymond James favors large caps over small caps, citing stronger EPS revisions and sector allocations.
October import prices rose 1.1% MoM, above expectations. Fuel prices rose 3.6% and nonfuel import prices rose 0.8%. Excluding food and fuel, prices rose 0.9%, the fastest pace in six months.
Import prices, CPI and PPI together suggest price pressures are broadening beyond energy. Raymond James expects a 25 bp Fed rate hike on December 9.

Hammack favored steady rate hikes. Musalem said a full 100 bps of tightening may be needed by spring. Schmid said containing inflation has become harder since Warsh's hawkish Jackson Hole speech in August. Warsh and Waller offered little guidance.
The 2-year Treasury yield at 4.80% sits more than 90 bps above the fed funds midpoint, which Raymond James views as an attractive entry point.

Indian equities are outperforming as AI-related stocks weaken. MSCI India (7.9% tech weighting) is up 9.2% MTD in local terms, and Bloomberg estimates nearly $10b of international fund inflows this month, above the Nov. 2000 record. Raymond James remains positive on India.

Growth and earnings prospects are improving, and the MSCI India Index has a low 7.9% tech weighting.
The 2-year yield at 4.80% is more than 90 bps above the fed funds midpoint, which Raymond James calls an attractive entry point.
